appraisal_events.evidence: un certain éclat dans ses yeux... faisait reluire autour du capitaine un incognito souverain; on tremblait quand il entrait dans le bureau du maréchal des logis chef... un regard capable de déjouer Talleyrand et tromper Alexandre
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator builds an elaborate portrait of Borodino as an incarnation of Napoleonic majesty who inspires awe even in trivial military-administrative matters, elevating him through grandiose historical association, though the disproportion with the mundane content mildly ironizes that elevation.

appraisal_events.evidence: à leur grande indignation ni le lieutenant-colonel, ni le médecin-chef, qui avaient si souvent dîné chez lui, ne reçurent plus, de toute leur vie, de ses nouvelles.
appraisal_events.explanation: After years of cultivated hospitality that flattered the bourgeois musician couples, Borodino drops them completely and permanently the moment he transfers away, revealing self-interested coldness beneath his gracious manner.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's awe-struck, quasi-imperial portrait momentarily elevates Borodino's aura of grandeur, though the effect is softened by comic hyperbole.
The abrupt, total abandonment of loyal bourgeois friends exposes self-serving coldness beneath his cultivated charm, lowering the local estimation of his character.

ambiguities: The Napoleonic-incarnation description mixes genuine narrator admiration with comic hyperbole (e.g., inspecting a soldier's trouser fabric with a gaze 'capable of outwitting Talleyrand'), so the elevation in E1 is not purely endorsed.
